MARINE AND FISHERIES TECHNOLOGY MARCH — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #10
====

GRADE: Grade 12
SUBJECT: MARINE AND FISHERIES TECHNOLOGY MARCH
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. A compound differs from a mixture because: (1 mark)
   A. A mixture always has a fixed melting point
   B. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya
   C. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio
   D. A compound can be separated by filtering only

2. Which change is a physical change? (1 mark)
   A. Ice melting to water
   B. Milk souring
   C. Paper burning to ash
   D. Iron rusting

3. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Technologies and Innovations in aquaculture? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Technologies and Innovations in aquaculture.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Technologies and Innovations in aquaculture.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Technologies and Innovations in aquaculture.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Technologies and Innovations in aquaculture.

4. In a food chain, green plants are usually: (1 mark)
   A. Primary consumers only
   B. Decomposers only
   C. Tertiary consumers
   D. Producers

5. Why is water unsuitable for a petrol fire? (1 mark)
   A. Water removes heat too quickly
   B. Water always increases oxygen
   C. Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely
   D. Petrol fires have no fuel

6. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Fish feeds and feeding? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Fish feeds and feeding.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Fish feeds and feeding.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Fish feeds and feeding.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Fish feeds and feeding.

7. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Record keeping in aquaculture? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Record keeping in aquaculture.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Record keeping in aquaculture.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Record keeping in aquaculture.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Record keeping in aquaculture.

8. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Fish Reproduction? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Fish Reproduction.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Fish Reproduction.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Fish Reproduction.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Fish Reproduction.

9. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Fish Ecology and Ecosystems? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Fish Ecology and Ecosystems.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Fish Ecology and Ecosystems.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Fish Ecology and Ecosystems.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Fish Ecology and Ecosystems.

10. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Weather and Climatic Conditions in Marine and Freshwater 3.3 Fishery by-products? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Weather and Climatic Conditions in Marine and Freshwater 3.3 Fishery by-products.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Weather and Climatic Conditions in Marine and Freshwater 3.3 Fishery by-products.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Weather and Climatic Conditions in Marine and Freshwater 3.3 Fishery by-products.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Weather and Climatic Conditions in Marine and Freshwater 3.3 Fishery by-products.

11. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Ornamental Fish culture? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Ornamental Fish culture.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Ornamental Fish culture.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Ornamental Fish culture.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Ornamental Fish culture.

12. Boiling point of pure water at standard pressure is about: (1 mark)
   A. 100 °C
   B. 0 °C
   C. 37 °C
   D. 50 °C

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Fish Reproduction and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Fish Ecology and Ecosystems and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Ornamental Fish culture and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Fish feeds and feeding and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
MARKING SCHEME
====

1. C — Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio

2. A — Ice melting to water

3. D — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Technologies and Innovations in aquaculture.

4. D — Producers

5. C — Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely

6. B — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Fish feeds and feeding.

7. A — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Record keeping in aquaculture.

8. A — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Fish Reproduction.

9. A — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Fish Ecology and Ecosystems.

10. D — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Weather and Climatic Conditions in Marine and Freshwater 3.3 Fishery by-products.

11. C — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Ornamental Fish culture.

12. A — 100 °C

Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Fish Ecology and Ecosystems; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

15. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Ornamental Fish culture; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

16. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Fish feeds and feeding; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
